title: Knowledge check: API Contracts and Change Management

questions.prompt: In API Contracts and Change Management, which statement best describes Documented schemas?
options: Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.

Connect this syllabus point to API Contracts and Change Management: state the expected behavior, identify a realistic edge case, and choose a test or observation that proves the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.
This option describes a different concept and does not define documented schemas (choice 2).
questions.answer_key: Connect this syllabus point to API Contracts and Change Management: state the expected behavior, identify a realistic edge case, and choose a test or observation that proves the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.
questions.explanation: Connect this syllabus point to API Contracts and Change Management: state the expected behavior, identify a realistic edge case, and choose a test or observation that proves the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying API Contracts and Change Management?
options: Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.
Separate HTTP handling from business rules, persistence, and integration clients. Dependency injection and consistent contracts make modules easier to test; avoid abstractions that hide control flow.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
questions.answer_key: Separate HTTP handling from business rules, persistence, and integration clients. Dependency injection and consistent contracts make modules easier to test; avoid abstractions that hide control flow.
questions.explanation: Separate HTTP handling from business rules, persistence, and integration clients. Dependency injection and consistent contracts make modules easier to test; avoid abstractions that hide control flow.

questions.prompt: A change related to API Contracts and Change Management appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
